title: Prism and lenses
prompt: an optical bench with a white lamp, a glass prism on a turntable and a screen, plus a converging and a diverging lens in holders: rotate the prism to split white light into a spectrum on the screen, swap in the converging lens and slide a candle object to see a real inverted image focus, swap in the diverging lens to see a virtual image, trace the rays; see-through shows the ray paths bending at each glass surface with refraction angles
blurb: Turn a glass prism to split white light, then focus a candle through two different lenses on an optical bench.
teachingNotes: Geometrical ray overlays use Snell refraction at the glass surfaces. Dashed backward extensions and the translucent upright candle mark a virtual image, which never appears on the screen. Flint-glass indices follow OpenStax Table 1.2. Spherical aberration is retained.
